messages:
min-seo-eng: Quick heads-up — planning to be in Seoul for ~4 weeks (2026-09-02 -> 2026-09-30) to help with family stuff. A few quick Qs before I submit the Temporary Location form: 1) Is the WFH stipend prorated for ~28 days abroad? 2) Im a US resident on Redwood payroll but have a Korean partner (non-Redwood)  any payroll/tax flags I should know about for a short stay? 3) I might need to bring my company laptop and a personal DSLR  any customs/export docs if I check the DSLR? 4) Any sign-off required for VPN/device access from Korea?

hana-peopleops: Hey Min-Seo, short answers: 1) Yes, stipends are prorated by calendar days for temporary moves under 90 days; 28 days will be prorated. 2) Submit the Temporary Location form with dates & address so we can kick off payroll/legal checks. 3) For devices: company laptop should be registered with IT and if you want us to ship it we must use ShipOps. Personal DSLR is your responsibility; if you check it in luggage, customs may ask for purchase proof. 4) IT approval: tag IT on the form and include device serials.

derek-payroll: Tagging in. Payroll notes: please confirm stipend currency (USD/KRW) and whether you need funds routed to a Korean bank. Stipends are taxed per your home payroll rules; short stays typically dont change tax residency (Korea uses 183-day rule), but any paid local work or contracting is a hard no. If your partnership involves a local employer contract, flag it. Well run a quick nexus check once form is submitted.

chae-legal: Quick legal add: South Korea also has withholding and social security considerations for certain activities, but for ~28 days on US payroll we usually clear. Two red flags: 1) in-person meetings where you sign deals or perform billable work for a Korean entity; 2) accepting paid gigs while there. Neither should be an issue for family care, but please list any planned meetings on the form. Also, keep copies of entry/exit stamps in case payroll/legal asks later.

it-ops: Security checklist:
```
- Register company laptop serial with IT before travel
- Ensure FileVault and screen lock enabled
- Bring YubiKey and set up offline MFA recovery
- Avoid using unsecured public Wi-Fi; use company VPN
- If you need to use a local SIM, request company eSIM stipend approval
```

hana-peopleops: Shipping note: If you want ShipOps to handle the company laptop, use shipops@redwood.com. We provide temporary export docs and up to $2k transit insurance for company devices. Personal camera/equipment shipped separately is not covered and may attract import duties. Link: https://redwood.company/hr/shipping-policy

min-seo-eng: Thanks  Ill submit the Temporary Location form today (dates & address) and attach the laptop serial. No client meetings planned  family care only. Ill carry the DSLR in my carry-on instead of checking it. Pref stipend in USD please.

hana-peopleops: Perfect  once the form is in well open a case and ping payroll/legal/IT. Also sounds like no gross-up will be necessary for a short stay.

ticket-bot: HR case created: HR-16890 "Temporary remote: Seoul 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-30 (Min-Seo)". Assigned to people-ops/hana.

min-seo-eng: Filing the form now and CCing my manager + IT. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
